_comment: Textures for materials the matcher cannot reach, and the interchangeable sets they belong to. texture_overrides.json is keyed on the texture stem an FBX asks for; this file is keyed on the FBX's own material name, which is the only handle on a material whose bitmap path was emptied before export. 'flavors' groups textures a pack ships as alternatives for one surface, either tileable variants of a surface or recolors of one atlas. 'bind' says which materials fall back to which set, matched on the model filename stem and on the material name, both optional. Those two are whole-name globs anchored at the start, so 'Wall*' means a material name beginning with Wall; this is deliberately unlike the 'flavors' member patterns above, which match the tail of a pack-relative path. Bindings are tried in order, first match wins, and only ever fill a channel that resolved to nothing. Keys starting with _ are ignored. Run --scan-materials --scan-report to see what is still bare in your own packs. 'companions' names the emissive and normal maps a pack ships for an atlas that no FBX references, because that wiring lived in Unity materials which are not part of the source packs. It is keyed on the atlas rather than on a material, since one emissive serves every material wearing that atlas and often every recolor of it too, so a key is a path-suffix glob that may match many textures while each channel's value must match exactly one. A companion only ever fills a channel that resolved to nothing, so a map the FBX named itself always wins.

PolygonFantasyKingdom._verification: Every binding below the first three was decided by importing the FBX in Blender, reading the mesh's own UV bounds, and sampling PolygonFantasyKingdom_01_A at those coordinates. Two patterns separate the atlas from the tileable Castle textures cleanly. A material whose UVs run past 1.0, typically V 1.00 to 1.99, is tiled onto a repeating surface and belongs to Wall; that is what SM_Bld_Castle_Wall_Block_01 to _05, the six SM_Bld_Castle_Wall_Cut_* and SM_Bld_Castle_Wall_03 to _05 all do, matching the V range of SM_Bld_Stairs_Round_M_Base_01, whose material really is called Wall. A material confined to a small island inside 0 to 1 is atlas mapped, and sampling names the color it was authored with: SM_Wep_Sceptre_02 draws gold 187,141,74 with a red gem 112,50,44, SM_Bld_Castle_Hoarding_Wood_Wall_01 draws three timber browns, SM_Prop_Gazebo_01 draws one flat 111,79,58 wood. Several cases have an exact twin that kept its binding. This pack ships every corpse twice, once as SM_Dead_* with the material stripped and once as SM_Prop_Dead_*: SM_Dead_Knight_01 and SM_Prop_Dead_Knight_01 have the same 6140 loops, the same U 0.014 to 0.254 V 0.007 to 0.736, and both sample steel 133,137,141, and SM_Prop_Dead_Knight_01 resolves to the atlas on its own. SM_Dead_Horse_04 and SM_Prop_Dead_Horse_04 share 2512 loops and produce an identical color histogram against Horse_01.png, which is what SM_Prop_Dead_Horse_04 resolves to. SM_Prop_Chair_Fancy_01 and _02 span the same island and sample the same gold and red. SM_Bld_Castle_Hoarding_Corner_L_01 and _M_01 span U 0.1516 to 0.4891 V 0.1555 to 0.6653, identical to Corner_S_01, which resolves. SM_Env_Bush_Cluster_01, _04, _05 and _06 span the same island as _02 and _03 and sample the same 71,83,56 green, so their PolygonApocalypse_Texture_01_Cleaned.psd reference is an artist's working file name rather than a real dependency. The SM_Bld_Preset_*_Optimized bodies span U 0.007 to 0.995 V 0.006 to 0.993, the footprint that identified the presets in the first place. Cases with no twin were checked against a UV coverage map built from 200 models that do resolve to the atlas: SM_Bld_Castle_Battlements_*_04, SM_Bld_Castle_Wall_Door_Big_01, SM_Prop_Gazebo_01 and SM_Prop_Hanging_Clothes_04 land 200 of 200 sampled points inside it. Flags are the one set whose choice is genuinely the consumer's: 21 SM_Prop_Flag_* models carry a single material naming Symbols.psd, which never shipped, and the 16 flags that did ship are one 1024 layout with the emblem centered and a pole, rope and timber swatch strip in the bottom left corner. SM_Prop_Flag_01 samples the white emblem and the blue field, while SM_Prop_Flag_18 to _20 and SM_Prop_Flag_Wall_Attachment_01 sit entirely in that swatch strip. Only the bottom row, V about 0.010, where SM_Prop_Flag_Wall_Attachment_01 sits, is pixel identical across all 16, the pole sampling 54, 59, 63 and the rope 83, 81, 81 exactly; the rest of the strip, V 0.010 to 0.039, which SM_Prop_Flag_18 to _20 cover, is the flag field color, which differs across color families, mean absolute difference 0.000 within a family and 26.4 to 65.0 across them. That difference is exactly the choice a consumer of a flavor set makes, so one 16 member set still stands, if anything better supported than before. Flag_Lion_01_Blue is the default because the crowned lion on teal is also the tile the pack's own atlas carries. The companions were settled by measuring every file the pack ships whose name reads as a map, and every pairing below is between two files of identical dimensions, 4096 by 4096 on the atlas and 2048 by 2048 on the tileable Castle sheets. All fifteen candidates measure as the channel they claim: the fourteen normals are 84.0 to 99.5 percent within 24 of 128,128,255 with means of 166.4 to 169.6 and 94.8 to 100 percent of their pixels blue dominant, and PolygonFantasyKingdom_01_Emmisive.png, which the worklist could not see until the detector learned Synty's doubled m, is 99.8 percent near black with a mean of 0.22 and 0.20 percent of the sheet lit. That emissive needs no inference. Its lit region is a single block at U 0.000 to 0.044 V 0.063 to 0.128, and along the top row of that block it carries five color fields whose boundaries fall at x 0, 36, 71, 107, 144 and 179 of 4096, while the atlas carries its own swatch strip at 0, 36, 72, 108, 144 and 179. Each of the five agrees in hue with the swatch beneath it: white 255,255,255 over gray 166,166,166 at 0.00 degrees, red 255,5,0 over 109,36,36 at 24.25, amber 255,179,0 over 111,80,38 at 15.54, green 63,254,4 over 53,114,35 at 18.26 and blue 0,132,255 over 49,62,83 at 26.89, against 50.28 to 66.21 degrees for any crossed pairing. That region is identical across all twelve Alts sheets, mean absolute difference 0.00 to 3.14, so one emissive serves any generation and the 01 family is the only one reachable. The two atlas normals are the case where the name decides nothing and the measurement reverses it. They are the same image everywhere except one tile: they differ on 3.73 percent of the sheet, that 3.73 percent lies entirely inside U 0.000 to 0.250 V 0.750 to 1.000, and in that tile PolygonFantasyKingdom_01_Normals.png is flat at a relief energy of 10.96 while _02_Normals.png carries brick courses at 33.81. Rendering the same tile across the twelve Alts sheets settles which is which: families 01, 02 and 03 all carry plain plaster there and only family 04 carries brick masonry, and _02_Normals' relief in that tile registers on 04_A, 04_B and 04_C at a two dimensional edge correlation of 0.301 to 0.315 and a row profile of 0.503 to 0.524 against 0.000 to 0.068 and 0.044 to 0.099 for all nine members of the other three families. So _01_Normals is the map for families 01, 02 and 03 and _02_Normals is the map for family 04, which is the reverse of what the numbering suggests. The three relief blocks the two maps share are what confirms both are atlas normals at all: stone brickwork at U 0.25 to 0.50 V 0.75 to 1.00, timber planking at U 0.00 to 0.25 V 0.50 to 0.75 and roof tiles at U 0.75 to 1.00 V 0.50 to 0.75, registering on the atlas at 0.312 to 0.332, 0.583 to 0.584 and 0.199 to 0.316 two dimensionally, identically on every generation because those three tiles are the same in all twelve. The five Wall normals each land on their own namesake and nowhere else, which makes the name correspondence here a finding rather than an assumption: relief against edge correlation of 0.545 for Wall_Brick_01_Normals, 0.455 for Wall_Dungeon_01_Normals, 0.431 for Wall_Evil_01_Normals, 0.356 for Wall_Large_Brick_01_Normals and 0.284 for Wall_Stucco_01_Normals on their own sheets, against 0.015 to 0.049 for every one of the twenty four other sheets the pack ships, so each takes its own key. The roofs are two layouts of four recolors each rather than eight sheets: Roof_Slat_01 through _04 agree with one another on 99.83 to 99.97 percent of their edge maps and Roof_Tile_01 through _04 on 99.30 to 99.83, while across the two families agreement drops to 96.80 to 97.64. Which normal serves which family is decided by structure, because the profile correlation used on the walls puts Roof_Slat_01_Normals nearer the Tile sheets, 0.147 against 0.064, and would have paired it wrongly. A slat sheet has no vertical divisions and a tile sheet has one per shingle, so the ratio of vertical to horizontal detail separates the two: 41.26 for Roof_Slat_01_Normals against 37.35 to 38.59 for the four Slat sheets, and 1.70 for Roof_Tile_01_Normals against 1.61 to 1.62 for the four Tile sheets, two ranges twenty three times apart with each map sitting inside its own family's. Course positions agree with that reading: six to seven of Roof_Slat_01_Normals' nine course lines fall within 3 pixels of 2048 of a Slat course line at a median offset of 1.0 pixel, against one of nine at a median of 15.0 on every Tile sheet, and seven of Roof_Tile_01_Normals' ten fall within 3 pixels of a Tile course at a median of 1.5, against none of ten at a median of 16.5 to 21.0 on every Slat sheet. One glob key per roof family, since within a family the four recolors score identically. The scan then shows the atlas emissive reaching 1978 models and the atlas normal only 1954, and the 24 model gap is not a miss: those are the twenty materials naming PolygonCastle_Texture_Normal_01.png, the two naming HouseRoofNormals.png and the two naming Woods_normals.png, none of which the pack shipped. A companion only fills a channel that resolved to nothing and an unresolved reference is not nothing, so those 24 keep the unresolved reference their own FBX declared and take the glow anyway.
PolygonFantasyKingdom._uncertain: Twelve SM_Bld_Castle_Pillar_Stone_* models share the material lambert22 and split down the middle: _03, _04, _Half_02, _Half_03, _Round_01 and _Round_02 sample the atlas's light stone 156,144,124 and sit inside its resolved coverage, while _01, _02, _Half_01, _Round_03, _05 and _05_Half either run past V 1.0 or scatter across unrelated swatches. Neither Wall nor Atlas is right for all twelve and no per model rule is defensible, so the family stays bare. The five SM_Bld_Castle_DestroyedWall_Rubble* pieces collapse to a single UV point: RubblePile_01 lands on stone gray 113,113,113, but Rubble_Top, _Middle and _Bottom land on 0,0,0 in the black padding along the atlas's bottom edge, and RubbleBlock_01 sits at V 1.1366. The seven flat wall pieces of that family tile normally and are bound; the rubble is not. FX_Sphere_03 samples one flat 113,113,113 and its sibling FX_Sphere does resolve to the atlas, but the point falls outside the coverage map and it is a single FX model, so it is left alone. Everything else still bare in this pack was never meant to carry a texture: the fountain water, the cloud ring, the two generic water planes, SM_Particle_Smoke_01, SunShafts, the candle flame and the flame cards of FX_Item_Candlestick_* and FX_Prop_Chandelier_*, all of which are one to thirty six loops spanning the whole of UV space. Six of the pack's fifteen companion candidates stay unbound. PolygonFantasyKingdom_02_Normals.png is the atlas normal for family 04, measured above, and nothing in this pack wears PolygonFantasyKingdom_04_A, _04_B or _04_C and no flavor set reaches them. The other five all belong to the Ground folder, which no material wears and no flavor set covers, so declaring any of them would be dead on arrival. Two are worth recording anyway, because the measurement disagrees with the name in the same way the roof pair nearly did: Sand_02_Normal.png correlates with Mud_02.png at 0.433 against Sand_02.png's 0.390, and Sand_03_Normals.png with Mud_03.png at 0.469 against Sand_03.png's 0.433, the sand and mud sheets of a given number being one layout in two palettes. Grass_02_Normals.png and Grass_03_Normals.png do land on their own namesakes, 0.388 against 0.220 for the runner up and 0.368 against 0.212. Ground_Base_01_Normals.png is a genuine tangent space normal, 99.3 percent within 24 of flat, but it correlates with nothing the pack ships above 0.093, so the sheet it was baked for never shipped.

POLYGON_Nature_Source_Files_v2._verification: The trees in this pack keep Trunk and Leave as separate materials on separate surfaces, so each half can be bound by name. Trunk means two different things and the UVs say which. On Pine, Willow, Generic and Dead trees the whole trunk collapses to a single UV point, which can only be a palette lookup: SM_Tree_Pine_01 sits at 0.168, 0.621 and samples PolygonNature_01 at 107,92,72, the same bark swatch the resolved SM_Tree_Pine_Base_01 reads at 0.180, 0.592, and SM_Tree_Dead_03 at 0.318, 0.602 samples 73,56,46, the swatch the resolved SM_Tree_Pine_Dead_01 reads at 0.315, 0.600. On the live birches the trunk is instead a real grid unwrap over the whole square, U 0.000 to 1.000 V 0.004 to 0.981 across 41 distinct face boxes, and Birch_Trunk_Texture.png is the pack's only full frame tileable bark and is bound by no model. Leave splits three ways by family. The six pines share six face boxes inside U 0.234 to 0.788, a centered band 0.554 wide, which is exactly where the conifer sprig sits in Leaves_Pine_Texture.png. Every willow leaf face is a single full square card, which only the full square willow drape fits. Birch and Generic have byte identical Leave layouts, five boxes split at V 0.429 and U 0.813, and Leaves_Generic_Texture.png is the only broadleaf cluster card shipped and is otherwise orphaned. Leaves_Dead is a different layout again, a 2 by 2 quadrant split, and Tree_Dead_Branch.png is the only bare branch card. SM_Plant_Bush_Leaves_03's Tree2 has exactly SM_Tree_Generic_01's Leave layout, 24 instanced full cards. PolygonNature_01 through _04 are one atlas recolored: their color discontinuity edge maps agree 100 percent. Every file this pack ships whose name reads as a map was measured and none of them is bindable, so this pack declares no companions and the eleven candidates are all accounted for in the note below. The measurement is what says so rather than the name: the eight Ground_Textures normals all register on their own namesakes, the two files with emissive in their names are coverage masks rather than glows, and the skybox normal is the only sheet in the pack besides the skybox diffuse that is not square.
POLYGON_Nature_Source_Files_v2._uncertain: The four River_Plane_* models are water and stay bare. Ground_Textures/Leaves.png and its _02 to _04 siblings really are four interchangeable recolors of one tileable leaf litter ground surface, and Grass_Textures/Grass_01 to _04 are four grass card variants, but no FBX in this pack has a bare ground or grass material, so neither would carry a binding and neither is declared. Worth a separate look: SM_Plant_Bush_Leaves_01 and _02, SM_Plant_Fern_* and SM_Plant_Undergrowth_01 are not bare but are almost certainly mis-resolved. They name a stale working path ending PolygonNature.png, which the matcher maps to the 512 pixel palette PolygonNature_01.png, while their UVs are full square alpha cards, so they render as confetti today. Their real textures, Leaves_Generic_Texture.png, Fern_Texture.png and Undergrowth_Texture.png, all ship and are orphaned. This file cannot reach them because their albedo already resolves; that is a texture_overrides.json job. None of the pack's eleven companion candidates could be bound, and the reasons split three ways. Eight are Ground_Textures normals, and each was placed before it was left alone: relief against edge correlation puts Flowers_normals.png on Flowers.png at 0.441 against 0.039 for the runner up, Pebbles_normals.png on Pebbles.png at 0.406, Mud_Normal.png on Mud.png at 0.388, Rockwall_Normal.png on Rockwall.png at 0.279 against 0.002, Cliffwall_normals.png on Cliffwall.png at 0.204 against 0.011, and Leaves_normals_01.png on the four interchangeable Leaves recolors at 0.098 to 0.133. Two of the eight are not merely orphaned by name: GrassHigherDetail_normals.png is 100.0 percent within 24 of 128,128,255, a map with no relief in it at all, and BaseGrass_normals.png is a genuine tangent space normal at 99.3 percent flat that correlates with nothing this pack ships above 0.110. All eight belong to the tileable ground and grass surfaces this file already declines to declare, since no FBX here has a bare ground or grass material, so none would ever reach a material or a generated sibling. The ninth is Skybox_Normal.png, which with Skybox_Diff.png is one of only two files in the pack at 8192 by 4096, a two to one panorama where every other sheet is square, so aspect ratio alone leaves it nothing but the skybox to belong to, and the pack ships no skydome model at all: its four bare materials are the four river planes. The last two are the pair the naming makes look like this pack's only emissives, and neither is one. Leaves_Willow_EmissiveTexture.png is 68.5 percent near black with 100 percent of its lit pixels gray, and its lit mask matches the alpha channel of Leaves_Willow_Texture.png at an intersection over union of 0.960, that card's alpha averaging 246.6 where the map is lit and 2.7 where it is dark. Inside the leaves it is the card's own luminance inverted, mean absolute difference from 255 minus the albedo of 2.96, which is why the two correlate at negative 0.957. That is coverage rendered as an image rather than a glow, and declaring it would make every willow drape shine flat gray. emissive.png is the same kind of file for a different card: 67.1 percent near black, 100 percent of its lit pixels gray, and its lit mask matches the alpha of Leaves_Generic_Texture.png at 0.976 against 0.088 to 0.457 for all thirteen other cards in the pack, with that card's alpha averaging 248.6 where it is lit and 0.1 where it is dark. Both cards carry real alpha of their own, mean 79.5 and 81.8, and both are declared cutout in the sets above, so the coverage these two files duplicate is already wired. The five _MaskTexture siblings the pack ships beside them carry nothing, their RGB means running 0.27 to 1.81 of 255.

POLYGON_NatureBiomes_AridDesert_SourceFi._verification: The eleven Alts recolors agree with PolygonNatureBiomesS2_AridDesert_Texture_01 on 99.98 to 100 percent of their edge maps, so they are one atlas in twelve palettes. The bindings are anchored on resolved siblings. The eight bare SM_Prop_Bones_* materials sit at U 0.355 to 0.362 V 0.120 to 0.154, and SM_Prop_Bones_06, whose Nature_Base_Mat4 resolves to the arid atlas, sits at U 0.355 to 0.361 V 0.125 to 0.154; one of the bare ones is literally named PolygonNatureBiomesS2_Alpine_Texture_01, a wrong biome placeholder. SM_Env_Rock_Cliff_16 sits at U 0.324 to 0.327 V 0.127 to 0.130 and its fifteen resolved siblings _01 to _15 all sit at U 0.324 to 0.327 V 0.126 to 0.130. SM_Env_Bush_Bramble_01's bare lambert2 has the identical bounding box, U 0.050 to 0.933 V 0.030 to 0.998, to the lambert9 on the same model that resolves to Branches_01.tga. SM_Env_Succulent_05's bare lambert13 spans U 0.040 to 0.964 over 44 face boxes against the 43 boxes of the SucculentLeaves_MAT02 on the same model that resolves to Succulent_Leaves_Diffuse_PNGTEMP.png. SM_Env_Succulent_03 spans U 0.005 to 0.916 over 193 boxes against the resolved SM_Env_Succulent_04's U 0.005 to 0.941 over 198. Cactus_01.tga is the pack's only cactus body sheet, four pads and a spine star, and rendering SM_Env_Cactus_01 with it gives a barrel cactus with orange spines where the atlas gives confetti. This is the one pack of the three that wires emission from its own FBX, on 77 materials, and that is what makes its companions checkable rather than merely plausible: the pack states two pairings itself, PolygonNatureBiomesS2_AridDesert_Emissive_01_A.png onto the atlas and Succulent_Leaves_03_normals.png onto Succulent_Leaves_03_.tga, plus Succulent_Flowers_01_normals.png onto Succulent_Flowers_01.tga, so every test used below was first run against those known answers and only trusted where it reproduced them. The twelve emissives and the twelve albedo sheets are all 4096 by 4096, and the maps share one fingerprint: 99.1 to 99.2 percent near black, means of 0.76 to 0.86, 0.77 to 0.89 percent of each sheet lit, and 7.6 to 8.8 percent of the lit pixels gray. They light the same pixels, pairwise lit mask intersection over union of 0.855 to 0.856 between Emissive_01_A and the other eleven, so this is one glow layout in twelve colorways and a glob across the family would be wrong. Which map belongs to which recolor is settled by color and not by name. Comparing each map's per pixel chromaticity against each albedo's inside that map's own lit mask gives a clean diagonal across all one hundred and forty four cells: every emissive sits 14.51 to 17.02 degrees from the sheet its name claims and 33.05 to 41.08 degrees from all eleven others, two ranges that do not touch, so each of the twelve is placed by a factor of two with no second candidate anywhere near. They are colored glow layers rather than lifted copies of the atlas, mean absolute difference 62.1 to 65.5 inside the lit mask against their own sheet and up to 92.0 against the worst, and the diagonal is lowest there too. Emissive_01_A is declared on the base sheet even though 77 materials already carry it from the FBX, because a companion only fills a channel that resolved to nothing: it changes nothing for those 77 and it stops the 01_A original from being the one member of the family with no glow while all eleven of its recolors have one. The card normals were settled per map, because this pack bakes them with padded backgrounds that defeat any single test, which the two known answers above are what proved. Where a map carries a real alpha mask, that mask is the answer: Grass_01_Normals.tga matches Grass_01.tga at an alpha intersection over union of 1.000 against 0.444 for the next card, Succulent_Leaves_02_normals.png matches Succulent_Leaves_02_.tga at 0.843 against 0.512, and the FBX wired Succulent_Flowers_01_normals.png scores 0.961 against 0.393 on the same test. Where the relief carries a hard silhouette, the map's strongest relief discontinuities land on the card's alpha edge: 0.934 for TumbleWeed_01_normals.png on TumbleWeed_01.tga against 0.368, 0.840 for TumbleWeed_01_Sphere_normals.png on TumbleWeed_01_Sphere.tga against 0.365, and 1.000 for Succulent_Flowers_01_normals.png and 0.551 for Succulent_Leaves_03_normals.png on the two the FBX already answers. Where neither works because the bake fills the whole frame, taking the flattest region of the map covering the same area as the card's alpha and measuring intersection over union puts Cactus_01_normals.png on Cactus_01.tga at 0.562 against 0.381, with Succulent_Flowers_01_normals.png scoring 0.850 against 0.387 as the control. Two maps are placed by shape read directly. Amplified three times, Cactus_01_normals.png carries three faceted cactus pads at upper left, lower left and lower right and an eight pointed spine star at upper right, which is Cactus_01.tga island for island. Succulent_Leaves_normals.png carries three saw toothed leaves with raised central midribs in three columns of decreasing width, matching Succulent_Leaves_Diffuse_PNGTEMP.png tooth for tooth, and distinguishing it from the smooth edged spears of Succulent_Leaves_02_.tga and the six rounded pods of Succulent_Leaves_03_.tga. AridDesert_GroundCover_01_normals.png carries starburst tufts at the same scattered positions as AridDesert_GroundCover_01.tga with the same tall thin wisps along the top edge, and it is that card that its row and column profiles favor at 0.52 and 0.60. The lava wave surface takes both channels. Its four albedo grades, Lavawave_Hot, Cold, Hot_Inverted and FlipTest, are within 0.8 to 8.8 mean absolute difference of one another, its three emissives within 0.6 to 3.9, and its two normals within 3.5, so this is one surface in near identical grades and the only question is which grade is worn: only Lavawave_Hot.png is, by nine models. Lavawave_Hot_Emissive.png sits 20.92 degrees from Lavawave_Hot.png in chromaticity against 50.34 from Lavawave_Cold.png, and it is 49.6 percent near black with a mean of 14.89, which is the right shape for lava rather than for a prop atlas since half the sheet is meant to glow. Side by side the three are unmistakably one set: the albedo is dark rock with red magma veins, the emissive is those same veins glowing orange on black in the same places, and Lavawave_normals.png is the same wave ridges in the same places, registering on that layout at 0.58 by row and 0.82 by column.
POLYGON_NatureBiomes_AridDesert_SourceFi._uncertain: Succulent_Leaves_03_.tga was deliberately left out of the SucculentLeaves set. Its alpha columns are up to 0.09 in UV away from the other two, and it is already the resolved texture for SM_Env_Succulent_01 and _02 over a different UV region, so including it would generate mis-registered swap variants. Everything else still bare here is excluded by kind: the sulfur pools, the pool and plane water, the fog ring, the skydome, the sun shafts and the smoke particle. lambert2024 was checked rather than assumed: its twelve faces span U 0.017 to 0.983 V 0.017 to 0.983, the same signature as SM_Env_Pool_Water_01, so it is the pool water plane. Sixteen of the pack's thirty six companion candidates stay unbound, and all but one because the albedo they belong to is worn by nothing and reached by no flavor set. Four are cards: AridDesert_Grass_01_normals.png, Cactus_03_LOD_normals.png, Succulent_04_LOD_normals.png and Succulent_06_LOD_normals.png, the last three being LOD billboards that no model in this pack binds. Nine belong to tileable ground, rock and lava sheets that nothing wears: Ground_Normals.png, which correlates at 0.75 with Sand_Texture_01, Sand_Texture_04 and Dirt_Texture_Arid_01 alike because those three are one layout recolored; RockWall_Normals_01.png, which has no RockWall albedo in this pack at all and lands on Rock_Texture_01 and _02 at 0.68 and 0.67; SaltCracks_normals.png on SaltCracks_Purple.png at 0.91 and 0.92; LavaRock_Normals.png on Lavarock_Texture.png at 0.89 and 0.87; Rock_Lava_Normals.png and Rock_Lava_Emission_01.png on Rock_Lava_Texture.png; Lavawave_FlipTest_Normals.png and Lavawave_FlipTest_Emissive.png on the FlipTest grade of the lava wave, which is a near duplicate of the Hot grade that is worn but is not itself worn; and BaseGrass_normals.png, which is a genuine tangent space normal at 99.3 percent within 24 of flat but correlates with nothing in the pack above 0.05, so its albedo never shipped. WaterNormals_01.png and _02.png belong to shader water with no material here. The sixteenth is a different case. Succulent_Leaves_03_normals 1.png is a second bake of the map the FBX already wires: amplified it is the same six pod layout as Succulent_Leaves_03_normals.png in the same positions, only with the relief dilated out past the silhouette, and the area matched test puts it on Succulent_Leaves_03_.tga at 0.561 against 0.385. That card already carries its own normal from the FBX, so declaring this copy would either do nothing or overwrite an answer the pack itself gave, and it stays out. One further file is worth naming because it never reaches the candidate list at all: Lavawave_Hot_Inverted_Emmissive.png is spelled with a doubled m, so companion_named does not recognize it as a map, and it is a real emissive, 49.9 percent near black with a mean of 11.39 and within 3.4 of Lavawave_Hot_Emissive.png. Nothing wears Lavawave_Hot_Inverted.png, so it would be unbound anyway, but the worklist is silent about it rather than knowingly leaving it.
